message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most significant and busiest airports across the United States:

| Airport | City / State | IATA Code | Notable Features |
|---------|--------------|-----------|------------------|
| **Hartsfield‑Jackson Atlanta International** | Atlanta, GA | ATL | Largest passenger hub worldwide; massive domestic & international traffic. |
| **Los Angeles International (LAX)** | Los Angeles, CA | LAX | Major West Coast gateway with extensive global connections. |
| **Chicago O’Hare International** | Chicago, IL | ORD | One of the world’s oldest hubs; high volume of flights and passengers. |
| **Dallas/Fort Worth International** | Dallas–Fort Worth, TX | DFW | Large mid-size hub connecting many U.S. cities. |
| **Denver International** | Denver, CO | DEN | Known as “The Mile High” airport; growing hub on the Rockies. |
| **John F. Kennedy International** | New York City, NY | JFK | Key East Coast hub with heavy transatlantic traffic. |
| **San Francisco International** | San Francisco, CA | SFO | Important West Coast hub especially for Asian routes. |
| **Seattle/Tacoma International** | Seattle, WA | SEA | Growing hub serving Pacific Northwest and Asia-Pacific. |
| **Miami International** | Miami, FL | MIA | Primary entry point into Latin America from the U.S. |
| **Orlando International** | Orlando, FL | ORF | Major leisure destination due to theme parks. |

These airports serve millions of travelers each year and act as critical nodes for both domestic and international air travel networks.
